description:
The Musée de l’Hôtel-Dieu in Mantes-la-Jolie grew from François-Victor Duhamel’s donation in 1913. Its collections bring the town’s history together with fine arts and decorative objects.

Medieval sculpture, stained glass and rare Hebrew gravestones are notable historical holdings. Paintings by Maximilien Luce and artists around him provide a later artistic focus.

description:
The Musée de l’Hôtel Sandelin in Saint-Omer developed from collections gathered by the town’s learned society in the nineteenth century.

Objects from regional religious institutions, architectural fragments and historic arms help explore the Audomarois. Broader collections of art and material culture reflect the varied interests of successive donors and collectors.

description:
The Musée de l’Image in Épinal is a public museum devoted to popular printed images. It is distinct from the historic commercial Imagerie d’Épinal.

Its collections include prints made in Épinal and other French centres, alongside examples from abroad. These images offer ways to study everyday beliefs, stories, entertainment and the circulation of visual culture.
